newsitem.title: USA: Almost all CIS states to record 1997 growth-IMF.
newsitem.headline: Almost all CIS states to record 1997 growth-IMF.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund expects growth in almost every country of the former Soviet Union this year, with the Transcaucasus republic of Georgia set to lead the way.

The IMF's World Economic Outlook said the Georgian economy would grow 10 percent, down just slightly from a strong 10.5 percent in 1996. Kyrgyzstan in Central Asia would record growth of 6.9 percent, after 5.6 percent in 1996.

"For a number of countries less advanced in transition, efforts at macroeconomic stabilization were rewarded in 1996 with sustained and sharp declines in inflation and, except for Russia and Ukraine, significantly improved growth performances," the IMF said.
It produced the following figures for countries belonging to the Commonwealth of Independent States, the loose grouping created when the Soviet Union fell apart.
